correctness.rationale: Every admissible finite graph diagram embeds in H_m by universality; homogeneity moves the embedded named base back onto A. An isomorphism fixing each named vertex and each corresponding tuple coordinate extends to an automorphism, so the full ordered injective types are exactly the labelled admissible diagrams, with no quotient by shore or tuple permutations. Since the old clique number is two, all diagrams are admissible with s<m−2, including the empty tuple. At r=m−2 a forbidden clique must use all r new vertices and an old adjacent pair, one from each part. It exists iff the new vertices form a clique and each old part contains a vertex with all-one incidence to the new clique. Counting incidence assignments on the two parts independently gives (q^a−h^a)(q^b−h^b); this counts a whole forbidden diagram once, regardless of how many old adjacent pairs witness it. Fix n from t_1=2^n (r>=2). Subtracting the corrections at (a+1,b−1) and (a,b) by expanding the cross terms gives (q−h)(qh)^a(q^(b−a−1)−h^(b−a−1)), strictly positive for b−a>=2 because q−h=1. Thus t_r strictly decreases along distinct steps toward balance. No shorter prefix separates K_{1,n−1} from K_{2,n−2} for n>=4; n=2,3 have unique positive unordered splits. The ambient is fixed throughout. Homogeneity makes every higher numerical count invariant under base isomorphism, with no canonical renaming required.
residual_risks: The full packaged finite diagnostic ranges were not independently rerun and are not necessary for the proof. No inference for arbitrary triangle-free bases or a varying ambient is intended.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader base family at arity two covers the particular low-arity counts where its ambient hypotheses apply; it does not reach the r-new-coordinate obstruction at m−2. Maximal multipartite or triangle-free ambient formulas have different old and new clique capacities and do not specialize to the distinct recovery claim.

value.rationale: Numerical tuple-type totals are natural invariants of pointwise named finite bases, and a biclique is the first family here with fixed clique number two but varying internal geometry at a fixed size. The theorem determines precisely when that geometry first becomes detectable from totals alone, gives quantitative separation between successive unordered sizes, and proves uniform impossibility below the threshold. The benign low-arity formula itself is routine; the value is the exact inverse boundary and spacing, potentially useful when comparing or calibrating reconstruction from finite extension counts.
residual_risks: Small elementary structural result; does not classify arbitrary bases, graded vs ungraded recovery generally, or reconstruction with unknown m.
